chunks: My father (RA) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Zakariyya, from Abu Basir, that Abu Abdillah (AS) said:

When a child of the believers passes away, a caller proclaims in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth: 'Verily, so-and-so's son has died.' If his father, mother, or one of them, or some of his family from among the believers have died, he is handed over to them to feed him. If not, he is handed over to Fatimah (peace be upon her) to feed him until his parents or one of them, or some of his family from among the believers arrive, and then he is handed over to them.

key_terms.مَلَكُوتِ: Kingdom or realm of the heavens

ai.seo_question: Who feeds a deceased child of believers in the afterlife according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* highlights the divine justice regarding children who die before reaching the age of accountability, illustrating their spiritual sustenance in the Barzakh. It emphasizes the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically Fatimah al-Zahra (AS), who acts as a spiritual guardian for orphans of believers, ensuring their nourishment until the reunion with their believing family. This underscores the Shia belief in the continuous spiritual care of the Imams and the Prophet's family even after death.
